projects.name: license-exam-prep
projects.title: License Exam Prep
projects.tagline: Designed and shipped an offline Python desktop application that prepares insurance agents for Florida state licensing exams across six license tracks.

detail.problem: Licensing is a revenue gate: new agents can't sell until they pass the state exam. The agency had no practice tool that could run on locked-down, carrier-managed workstations with no add-ins, macros or cloud installs.
detail.solution: Owned the product end to end, from requirements to deployment. The result is a single-file Windows executable (Python, PyWebView, SQLite, ReportLab). It runs full-length timed exams mapped to the official Pearson VUE Florida content outlines, and adds a projected-score gauge, per-domain mastery analytics and branded PDF performance reports.
highlights: Built a 1,467-question, outline-mapped item bank (500 hand-written master items) across six license tracks: 2-20, 20-44, 4-40, 2-15, 2-14 and 2-40
Architected blueprints as data: exam weights are validated at startup, so outline changes need no code change or redeploy
Integrated an LLM (Anthropic API) for AI-generated study narratives, with the API key DPAPI-encrypted at rest and a deterministic offline fallback
Quality gate: 17 automated tests passing (verified 2026-09-22)
detail.diagram:
flowchart LR UI[Web UI
index.html + app.js] -- js_api --> API[api.py] API --> ASM[assembler.py
blueprint-weighted sampling] ASM --> BANK[(data/banks/*.json)] ASM --> BP[(blueprints.json)] API --> DB[(SQLite attempts)] DB --> PROJ[projection.py
recency-weighted mastery] API --> RPT[reports_ai.py / reports_pdf.py] RPT -->|optional| ANT[Anthropic API] RPT --> PDF[PDF report]
notes: Question content is original training material written to the public content outlines; it is not sourced from secured exam items.
Logo files in `web/assets/` are neutral placeholders.

projects.name: training-program
projects.title: Agency Training Program
projects.tagline: Built an internal learning management system (LMS) that standardizes staff onboarding with video modules, randomized assessments, remediation gates and automated manager reporting.

detail.problem: Training was scattered across decks and videos, with no assessment tracking and no manager visibility into results. That made onboarding inconsistent and hard to hold people accountable to.
detail.solution: Designed and delivered a content-driven training platform. Each module (video, slides, chapters, question bank and Core Process document) is data, added through a built-in import wizard with no code change or rebuild, so non-technical staff can publish training.
highlights: Engineered a randomized assessment engine: round-robin draws across sections, with shuffled questions and answer options on every attempt
Enforced mastery: a failed attempt triggers a server-enforced remediation gate, so staff must rewatch the sections they missed before retaking
Automated score reporting to the right manager through Outlook COM, working around a tenant that blocks SMTP AUTH; failed sends queue in SQLite and retry
Added in-app PDF.js document viewing and cross-content search across narration, slides, documents and links
Quality gate: 39 automated tests passing (verified 2026-09-22), plus a Playwright end-to-end suite for the web variant
detail.diagram:
flowchart LR W[Import wizard] -->|PPTX→PNG via PowerPoint COM
quiz draft via Claude API| C[(content/module folders)] C --> M[modules.py
schema validation] M --> UI[Web UI + search] UI --> Q[scoring.py
bank draw + remediation] Q --> DB[(SQLite)] Q --> P[reports_pdf.py] P --> E[emailer.py
Outlook COM / SMTP + retry queue] UI --> S[server.py
localhost Range server for video seek]
notes: `content/` (training videos and decks) and `config/roster.json` are not in the repo; the roster in `koi_training/roster.py` is fictional.
`web-portal/` holds a later browser-based variant (single HTML page + PHP roster API) and its Playwright end-to-end test.

projects.name: filegate
projects.title: FileGate — Naming Compliance Auditor + AI Intake
projects.tagline: Built and deployed an AI-powered data-governance platform that audits about 67,000 client files against policy and files new documents automatically using LLM field extraction.

detail.problem: Client records on the shared file server had drifted from the agency's naming and folder policy, which hurt retrieval and created compliance and E&O risk. No one could see where violations were or who owned them.
detail.solution: Designed, built and put into production a two-part system. The Naming Compliance Auditor encodes the data policy as a machine-readable ruleset, attributes file ownership, locks a baseline compliance score per employee and supports reversible renames. FileGate Intake is an automated document-ingestion pipeline: staff upload a file and an on-site agent uses LLM extraction (Claude API) to identify the client, document type and address, renames it to policy and files it.
highlights: Treated policy as code (versioned JSON ruleset); anything that can't be derived goes to a human review queue instead of being guessed

Ran a root cause analysis on stalled weekly scans: throughput fell from about 178 items/s on the office LAN to about 7 over the VPN. Fixed it with a network gate, incremental commits and explicit failure states, then migrated the job to an always-on host
Production scan: 67,240 items processed in 24 minutes with 0 errors (2026-09-22)
Human-in-the-loop design: unmatched documents are parked for review, never mis-filed
Quality gate: 62 automated tests passing; a 388,000-row database migration verified before go-live
Drove adoption with change-management deliverables: a 33-slide training deck, two narrated videos, a 24-question assessment and two SOPs (2026-09-24)
notes: Completed: in production since 2026-09-23. Compliance-rate improvement will be published once rename cycles begin.

projects.name: uw-triage
projects.title: UW Triage Engine + Board
projects.tagline: Automated the underwriting-notice workflow end to end: LLM-powered triage, a web-based work board and two-way Slack integration for accountability and SLA tracking.

detail.problem: Carrier underwriting notices arrived by email and fell through the cracks. There was no single source of truth for what was due, who owned it, or what was past due, which put policies and client retention at risk.
detail.solution: Built an intake-to-resolution pipeline. An Apps Script engine monitors the notices mailbox, uses the Claude API to extract structured fields, and writes work items to a central tracker. A web-app board lets agents claim and close items, with Slack DMs, a daily digest and commands issued straight from Slack threads.
highlights: Shipped iteratively through board v2.10.5 and engine v1.4, including backfill of legacy notices
Built two-way Slack integration within platform constraints (polling, since Apps Script can't read Slack signing headers), with every write going through one controlled path
Standardized SLA visibility: one Past Due flag measured in days, plus an end-of-day digest
Regression suites recorded 0 failures at v2.10

projects.name: audit-system
projects.title: Audit & Compliance Scoring System
projects.tagline: Architecting a self-hosted quality-assurance and compliance audit platform: statistical sampling, rubric-based scoring, issue tracking and BI dashboards.

detail.problem: Policy-file quality was checked ad hoc, with no sampling method, no scoring rubric and no audit trail, so QA results couldn't be defended or trended.
detail.solution: Designing a zero-license-cost, self-hosted stack on the office NAS (Docker): seeded stratified sampling, a versioned YAML scoring rubric, human-in-the-loop checklists (Jotform) feeding n8n workflows, findings stored in PostgreSQL, and Metabase dashboards for leadership reporting.
highlights: Pure, unit-tested scoring and sampling functions
Designed the database schema and migrations (000–003), including a unified issue model for scheduled audits and reactive intake
Built for a hard constraint: the carrier portal allows no automation, so about 30–40% of checks stay human-in-the-loop by design

projects.name: apps-script-toolkit
projects.title: Apps Script Toolkit
projects.tagline: A suite of Google Apps Script automations that replaced manual reporting and scattered tools: KPI and SLA tracking, assessment generation, spend-data import and a team portal.

detail.problem: Operations reporting and staff tools lived in manual spreadsheets and bookmarks, and the carrier-managed Microsoft 365 environment blocks macros and add-ins.
detail.solution: Delivered focused automations in the Google environment the agency is permitted to automate, cutting manual work in reporting, training and finance tracking.
highlights: KPI tracker: computes business-hours SLA metrics (Mon–Fri, 8 AM–6 PM), generates weekly roster rows and refreshes every 10 minutes
Assessment generator: builds five auto-graded Google Forms with shuffled choices and per-item feedback
Spend tracker: CSV import, formula repair and a custom menu for a multi-source spend workbook
Quick-Launch Hub: a web-app portal embedded in the team intranet (v1.2, 2026-09-22)

projects.name: training-video-pipeline
projects.title: Narrated Training Video Pipeline
projects.tagline: Automated training-video production: turns slide decks and scripts into narrated MP4s with AI text-to-speech and interactive HTML players with clickable links.

detail.problem: Slide-deck training wasn't self-serve, recording narration by hand didn't scale, and MP4 files can't carry clickable links to the tools being taught.
detail.solution: Engineered a scripted production pipeline: slides are rendered to images, narration is synthesized per slide with neural text-to-speech, segments are assembled with FFmpeg, and an HTML player overlays time-synced link hotspots on the video.
highlights: Produced and shipped six training videos in two days (2026-07-14 to 2026-07-15) across three software rollouts
Placed hotspots automatically from slide-shape bounding boxes (python-pptx)
Built in quality controls: pronunciation rules for acronyms and product names, and every segment validated with ffprobe before assembly

slide PNGs] SCR[docs/narration-*.md] --> SEG[src/segments_tts.json] SEG --> TTS[src/tts_generate.py
edge-tts per segment] PNG --> FF[ffmpeg segment encode] TTS --> FF FF --> MP4[Video MP4] MP4 --> PL[players/player-*.html
time-synced link overlays]

projects.name: design-system
projects.title: Design System
projects.tagline: Created a design system (design tokens plus a React component library) to enforce brand consistency and WCAG AA accessibility across web properties.

detail.problem: Web pages and generated materials drifted from the brand, with no shared source of truth for color, type or components.
detail.solution: Established one source of truth: CSS design tokens mirrored into a JavaScript theme and Tailwind config, consumed by a reusable React component library and documented in a usage guide.
highlights: Defined palette, type scale, spacing, radius and elevation tokens with WCAG AA contrast rules
Delivered 10 reusable components (Badge, Button, Card, Footer, Hero, Input, NavBar, QuoteCTA, ServiceTile, Testimonial), barrel-exported for easy adoption

flowchart LR
  T[src/tokens.css] --> J[src/theme.js]
  T --> TW[tailwind.config.js]
  T --> C[src/components/*.jsx]
  C --> P[preview.html]
notes: Brand logo URLs were replaced with a placeholder.

projects.name: sdr-talk-path
projects.title: SDR Talk Path Companion
projects.tagline: Built a sales-enablement tool: an interactive call-guidance widget that gives sales development reps (SDRs) consistent, situation-specific cross-sell talk paths.

detail.problem: New SDRs needed consistent, situation-specific call guidance for cross-sell conversations.
detail.solution: Designed a self-contained JavaScript/HTML widget with talk paths for each client situation (for example auto-only, home-only or renter), plus keyword search and routing guidance. It's deployed on the company CMS.
highlights: Shipped in three delivery formats for CMS flexibility: Elementor embed (v1.1), Elementor widget (v1.2) and a WPCode JavaScript snippet (v1.2)

projects.name: pfsense-wireguard-vpn
projects.title: Secure Remote Access — pfSense Firewall + WireGuard VPN
projects.tagline: Designed, deployed and administer the agency's perimeter firewall and zero-cost WireGuard VPN, enabling secure remote access for a hybrid workforce of 20+ users.

detail.problem: Remote and hybrid staff needed secure access to on-premises resources (file server and printers), but the agency had no managed firewall or VPN, and staff laptops don't grant local admin rights.
detail.solution: Procured and deployed a Netgate 2100 running pfSense as the network perimeter, with WireGuard as the single standardized VPN. The rollout was engineered so non-admin users can connect and disconnect on their own, without weakening endpoint controls.
highlights: Procured the Netgate 2100 (October 2025) and brought the VPN into production in December 2025
Onboarded 20+ remote and in-office users
Achieved non-admin enablement: WireGuard deployed as a Windows service with a least-privilege network-operator role (January 2026)
Built VPN access revocation into the employee offboarding checklist (access governance)
Led incident response: diagnosed and resolved a server-side issue blocking remote access to on-prem systems (August 2026)
Benchmarked file-share throughput over the VPN against the LAN, and used the data to move bulk workloads on-network
notes: Network specifics (addresses, interfaces, peers) are intentionally omitted.

projects.name: qnap-nas
projects.title: Agency File Server — QNAP NAS as System of Record
projects.tagline: Led the business case, procurement and deployment of a centralized network-attached storage (NAS) system that became the agency's system of record for client data.

detail.problem: Client files were scattered across personal drives and laptops, creating data-loss, privacy and E&O exposure and slowing retrieval.
detail.solution: Ran a vendor evaluation, secured owner approval and deployed a QNAP TVS-h674 on QuTS hero (ZFS) with two 4 TB WD Red drives in RAID 1. It has per-employee accounts, a designed folder-permission model, a least-privilege service account for automation, VPN-based remote access and quarterly backups.
highlights: Evaluated three NAS platforms across price and capability tiers and presented a recommendation to ownership (July 2025)
Authored the FY2026 Technology Budget Proposal, including the storage line item (October 2025)
Procured in October 2025; built and brought to production in-office (November–December 2025)
Improved data resilience: mirrored storage (RAID 1) plus a quarterly backup cadence
Applied least-privilege access: a file-sharing-only service account for automation
Consolidated about 67,000 client-file items under a weekly automated compliance scan (see FileGate); the NAS also hosts the staff training web platform
notes: Share names, addresses and accounts are intentionally omitted.

projects.name: remote-print-server
projects.title: Remote Printing Service
projects.tagline: Deploying a centralized print service that lets hybrid staff print securely to office printers from anywhere over the VPN.

detail.problem: Staff could print only while physically in the office, which slowed remote and hybrid workflows.
detail.solution: Stood up an office print server that shares the agency printers over the VPN, and wrote a one-page self-service setup guide to cut support tickets.
highlights: Live since August 28, 2026 for the office's shared printers; remaining printers being reconnected
Published a self-service setup guide (v1.1): connect the VPN, open the print server, add a printer
Resilient by design: jobs sent while offline queue and release when the VPN reconnects
notes: In progress. Next milestone: remote staff setup and testing, then a training SOP and Core Process module.

projects.name: it-department
projects.title: Establishing the Agency IT Department
projects.tagline: Built the agency's IT function from the ground up: technology budget, procurement, vendor management, IT service desk, device lifecycle and systems governance.

detail.problem: The agency had no IT function. Purchasing, vendors, support and equipment were handled ad hoc, with no budget, no service levels and no systems inventory.
detail.solution: Established a dedicated IT operations function: an annual technology budget, a centralized systems and vendor ledger, a tiered support model with a defined response SLA, and a managed device lifecycle.
highlights: Career progression: Licensed Sales Producer, then a home-insurance sales seat, then promoted to Technical Solutions Manager (August 2025; full-time November 2025) and Agency Operations & Systems Manager (April 2026)
Authored and own the FY2026 Technology Department Budget
Launched a standardized equipment-request intake with a weekly procurement cycle (November 2025)
Designed a tiered IT service desk: an AI support chatbot as first line, escalating to an IT request form with a 1-business-day response SLA
Built a centralized systems ledger tracking 81 tools; System Administrator for 41
Own onboarding and offboarding, device imaging and a secure wipe, recycle and donation pipeline

projects.name: asset-inventory
projects.title: Asset Inventory & Storage System
projects.tagline: Implemented IT asset management (ITAM): a tagged inventory of 150+ items with labeled storage and a remote-equipment register.

detail.problem: Equipment was untracked and scattered across desks and homes, creating loss risk, duplicate purchases and slow replacements.
detail.solution: Created an asset-management system: numbered asset tags, label-maker labeling, a central register on the agency file server, labeled storage, and a register of agency-owned equipment held by remote staff.
highlights: Tracks 150+ assets, including cords and cables
Standardized tagging with numbered asset codes and PT label-maker labels
Centralized the asset register on the agency file server
Captured serial, brand and model for agency equipment held by remote staff
Ran a return-to-pool reclamation drive to recover unused equipment (December 2025)
Reorganized storage with labeled bins and new cube shelving (August 2026)

projects.name: shipping-station
projects.title: Shipping & Postage Station
projects.tagline: Stood up and modernized an in-office shipping and postage operation, then migrated it to a Zebra thermal printer and Shippo multi-carrier platform when the legacy hardware failed.

detail.problem: Packages and postage required trips out and manual label handling. Later, the legacy Pitney Bowes printer failed out of warranty.
detail.solution: Built an in-office shipping station, then led a vendor migration from Pitney Bowes to a Zebra ZD421 thermal printer with Shippo for multi-carrier labels. USPS stamps are purchased on demand through Stamps.com and printed in batches to control recurring cost.
highlights: Implemented Pitney Bowes shipping labels and scale (November 2025)
Migrated to a Zebra ZD421 plus Shippo after the out-of-warranty hardware failed (April 2026)
Controlled recurring cost: Stamps.com used on demand, with stamps printed in batches and the subscription cancelled between uses
Reconciled postage charges against card statements with no discrepancies

projects.name: ups-backup-rollout
projects.title: UPS Battery-Backup Rollout
projects.tagline: Led a business-continuity rollout of battery backup across every office desk and every remote employee's internet connection.

detail.problem: Power interruptions took down office workstations and network equipment, and remote staff lost connectivity during outages.
detail.solution: Standardized battery backup: a CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD UPS at each office desk, a UPS on the office modem/router, and a Daran 89.6 Wh LiFePO4 portable power station for each remote employee's modem and router.
highlights: Deployed one CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD UPS per office desk for workstation continuity
Protected the office network edge with a dedicated modem/router UPS
Equipped every remote employee with a Daran 89.6 Wh LiFePO4 power station (100 W), sourced with spares at a volume discount (September 2026)
Extended the life of legacy units by sourcing exact replacement batteries
Ran a fire-code compliance review (NFPA 1, Florida Fire Prevention Code, UL guidance) and defined five compliant installation options

projects.name: supply-subscriptions
projects.title: Office Supply Management — Subscription Ordering
projects.tagline: Centralized procurement by moving recurring office supplies from ad-hoc orders to managed subscription purchasing with a shared request queue.

detail.problem: Supplies were ordered ad hoc, one request at a time, with no central control or visibility.
detail.solution: Implemented subscription-based purchasing on Amazon Business Subscribe & Save, with a shared request cart so staff queue needs instead of placing one-off orders.
highlights: Automated replenishment of recurring items such as drinks, snacks and printer paper
Replaced one-off orders with a shared request queue
Centralized account administration and purchasing control
notes: Active since about May 2026. Spend tracking through QuickBooks is planned for Q4 2026.
